    get:
      description: Returns a paginated list of dashboards. Each result includes title, description, tags, and metadata, but not the full panel layout. Use `GET /api/dashboards/{id}` to retrieve the complete state.
      operationId: get-dashboards
      parameters:
        - description: The page of results to return.
          in: query
          name: page
          required: false
          schema:
            default: 1
            minimum: 1
            type: number
        - description: The number of results to return per page.
          in: query
          name: per_page
          required: false
          schema:
            default: 20
            maximum: 1000
            minimum: 1
            type: number
        - description: Filters results by `title` and `description` using Elasticsearch [`simple_query_string`](https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/query-languages/query-dsl/query-dsl-simple-query-string-query) syntax. Multi-word terms require all words to match.
          in: query
          name: query
          required: false
          schema:
            type: string
        - description: A tag ID to include. Accepts a single tag ID or multiple tag IDs. When multiple are specified, library items matching any of the tag IDs are included.
          in: query
          name: tags
          required: false
          schema:
            default: []
            description: Tag IDs associated with this dashboard.
            items:
              maxLength: 250
              type: string
            maxItems: 100
            type: array
        - description: A tag ID to exclude. Accepts a single tag ID or multiple tag IDs. When multiple are specified, library items matching any of the tag IDs are excluded.
          in: query
          name: excluded_tags
          required: false
          schema:
            default: []
            description: Tag IDs associated with this dashboard.
            items:
              maxLength: 250
              type: string
            maxItems: 100
            type: array
        - description: A tag name to include. Accepts a single tag name or multiple tag names. When multiple are specified, library items matching any of the tag names are included. If the same name is shared by multiple tags, items matching any of those tags are included.
          in: query
          name: tag_names
          required: false
          schema:
            items:
              type: string
            maxItems: 100
            type: array
            x-state: Generally available; added in 9.6.0

          in: query
          name: excluded_tag_names
          required: false

            items:

            type: array

I created the dashboard and the alert rule, and the rule is enabled. It has already run once successfully and fired no alerts.

**1. What the data holds.** The data view `Kibana Sample Data Logs` uses `timestamp` as its time field. Each document is one web request. The main fields are:
- **Request:** `clientip`, `url`/`request`, `extension`, `referer`, `agent`
- **Response:** `response` (the HTTP status, stored as text with a `.keyword` version) and `bytes` (response size)
- **Location:** `geo.src`, `geo.dest`, `geo.coordinates`
- **Client machine:** `machine.os`, `machine.ram`, plus `host` and `tags`

Across the whole index, response codes are 200 (12,832), 404 (801) and 503 (441).

**2. Dashboard: `EFF-e8f8c89b Web logs overview`** (id `ba9166c4-2409-48c9-b56f-68d7ba826f3a`, default time range last 7 days). It has six panels:
- Total requests
- Unique visitors (distinct client IPs)
- Average response size in bytes
- Error rate: the share of 4xx and 5xx responses (8.82% across all data)
- Requests over time as stacked bars, split by response code
- Top 10 requested URLs

I ran the queries behind the error-rate and top-URLs panels, plus a count by response code, directly against Kibana and they returned the expected results. I checked through the API that the dashboard is saved with all six panels, but I haven't opened it in the browser.

**3. Rule: `EFF-e8f8c89b 5xx spike`** (id `2e6ce657-02a2-4282-a84e-4ca0f93e756d`). It's an Elasticsearch query rule on `kibana_sample_data_logs`:
- It runs every minute.
- It matches requests whose response code starts with 5 (the `response.keyword` field).
- It fires when more than 10 of them arrive within 5 minutes, measured by `timestamp`.

The rule has no actions attached, so when it fires the alert only appears in Kibana; nobody is notified. If you want emails or other notifications, a connector needs to be added.

The request files I used are in the scratchpad as `dash.json` and `rule.json`.
